title: Possible cylinder expansion-vessel problem | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand possible cylinder expansion-vessel problem. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: Repeated pressure-related discharge can suggest an expansion issue, but the vessel, circuit and manufacturer requirements must first be identified.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: A heating-circuit vessel and a potable-water cylinder vessel are not interchangeable. Concealed vessels or multiple expansion components may be present on some products. Colour and location alone are not a reliable diagnosis.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: Record the equipment labels and discharge timing. Checking or adjusting a vessel requires a competent procedure for the actual system, not a universal pressure copied from another product.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can a boiler expansion vessel cure a domestic-water expansion problem?
faqs.answer: Not as a general substitution. The circuits, vessel suitability and design differ; competent assessment must identify the expansion provision needed.
